lanes.summary: Jev is reachable from Python over plain HTTPS POST plus JSON with a bearer token, no Node needed. Four routes exist and all were confirmed live by unauthenticated probes. (A) Vercel's documented HTTP API, POST https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/evaluate, body {model:"typesafe-ai/jev", state, questions, providerOptions?}, types choice/score/boolean, camelCase usage. (B) Vercel's TypeSafe-compatible API, POST https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/typesafe/v1/systemone, same body but booleans are type "noul", snake_case response. (C) the AI SDK internal protocol, POST https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v4/ai/evaluation-model, model in header ai-model-id, plus mandatory ai-gateway-protocol-version: 0.0.1, ai-evaluation-model-specification-version: 4, ai-gateway-auth-method: api-key|oidc; body has no model field. (D) TypeSafe direct, POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, model "jev-latest", public OpenAPI, official Python SDK typesafe-sdk 0.7.0. API key and OIDC both travel as Authorization Bearer; OIDC tokens last 12 hours and suit only Vercel deployments. Confidence is not inside gateway answers: it lives at providerMetadata.typesafe.confidence, while the direct API returns it inline. Probabilities are rounded to two decimals. Limits: 64k tokens per request, 32k for state plus the longest question, 255 choice options, 10 score levels, 1,200 RPM direct. Both hosts speak HTTP/2. Local network floor: gateway edge (Paris) 220 to 280 ms cold, 62 to 82 ms warm; api.typesafe.ai is in AWS us-west-2, 180 ms warm. Vendor claims 111 to 114 ms round trip; Vercel publishes no Jev latency. Vendor docs admit small run to run noise on some booleans, so Jev is stable, not strictly deterministic.
lanes.recommendation: Write our own thin async Python JevClient on httpx with http2 enabled (add httpx[http2]; system Python has httpx 0.28.1 but no h2) instead of shelling to Node or adopting typesafe-sdk in the hot path. Speak the TypeSafe wire shape and default to the gateway's TypeSafe-compatible route, POST https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/typesafe/v1/systemone with Authorization: Bearer AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and model "typesafe-ai/jev". That honours the user's requirement to go through the Vercel AI Gateway, is publicly documented, needs only two headers, and is byte compatible with the direct API, so switching to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (key TYPESAFE_API_KEY, model jev-latest, or a pinned jev-1.13.0) is a three value config change that gives us a fallback path and an A/B latency comparison. Keep a second small adapter for the documented /v1/evaluate route (boolean/probability naming, confidence under providerMetadata.typesafe.confidence) in case Vercel favours it. Do not build on the internal /v4/ai/evaluation-model route: it is version gated by header, undocumented and flagged as changeable in patch releases; use the package source only as a schema reference. Transport policy for the voice loop: one persistent connection, warmed on daemon start and on push to talk or wake word (the unauthenticated GET /typesafe/v1/models works as a free warm-up and saves about 200 ms measured), hard deadline near 1.5 s, at most one immediate retry on connection reset or 5xx/529, honour retry-after on 429 but surface busy in the UI rather than blocking, no exponential backoff. Put every speculative question in a single request (vendor docs and the smart home demo show fan-out is nearly free and answer independent). Treat probabilities as two decimal values, never require sums of exactly 1, and gate actions with margins plus the separate confidence statistic because the vendor admits small run to run noise on booleans. Plan for roughly 200 to 350 ms per decision from this European location until a real key lets us measure; do not promise the vendor's 111 ms figure. First task once a key exists: a 50 call benchmark of routes A, B and D over a warm HTTP/2 connection, and a check that confidence and legend are returned on A and B.

lanes.summary: Jev question design is well documented in primary sources: docs.typesafe.ai exposes a full dump (llms-full.txt) including a vendor-written failure mode page for jev-1.13, and Vercel ships evaluation docs inside the ai npm package. Core rules: send one request per utterance with many atomic questions (evaluated independently, state ingested once, extra questions cost only their tokens); write literal, direct instructions with each speculative premise stated; describe options and score levels as situations, using contrastive objects (what, not_for, examples) only for confusable pairs; keep state small, named JSON because Jev suffers context rot; never ask Jev to count, do math, compare numbers, or generate text. Slot filling follows TypeSafe's function calling cookbook: intent Choice plus one Choice per closed-set slot plus a "stated" Noul per optional slot, candidates found in code offered as options, and command confidence taken as the minimum across judgments. A Choice is relative and always picks something, so pair it with a none option or an absolute Noul. Confidence appears to equal (p_max - 1/n)/(1 - 1/n), my inference fitting 15 documented examples, so gate on probabilities and top-two margin. Gate per action class with act, confirm, reject bands; vendor examples use 0.6 floors and 0.85 to 0.9 for risky actions. Jev is not strictly deterministic: TypeSafe's own repeats show 90.8 percent raw label agreement on a borderline input. English is the primary language; nothing exists on noisy ASR. Cost is negligible (about 250 token fixed overhead, $0.042 per 1M input). Independent evidence is thin but mostly positive on calibration at the extremes. Python can call the Gateway directly over HTTP.
lanes.recommendation: Design the Jev layer as one fan-out request per utterance, modeled on TypeSafe's function calling cookbook and smart home demo. State: a small named JSON object with a note explaining that utterance is an ASR transcript and that desktop is reference data only, the utterance (plus n-best alternatives if available), a pruned desktop snapshot (windows as short records with IDs w1..wN, capped around 40, titles truncated, no raw geometry), and code-generated candidate lists (fuzzy or phonetic prefiltered app names, numbers parsed from number words). Questions in the same request: is_command Noul (also usable for endpointing on partial transcripts), intent Choice of 30 to 60 situational options including none and unclear, target_window Choice over window IDs plus focused and none with a window_stated Noul, one premise-stated Choice per closed-set slot (workspace, direction, app, magnitude, toggle), and is_destructive, is_compound and is_correction Nouls. Read only the slots of the winning intent. Only click-in-app intents get a second request with the chosen window's pruned a11y controls (cap near 60) as options. Put a deterministic grammar fast path in front for exact commands and keep it as the fallback behind a 600 to 900 ms deadline; keep one warm HTTP/2 connection, one request in flight, sequence numbers, stale discard, backoff on 429/529. Gate in code by risk class using min over consumed judgments: reject below about 0.5, act on navigation at 0.6, reversible changes at 0.75, destructive only at 0.9 plus a lexical guard and confirmation otherwise; compute top-two margin from probabilities to drive a numbered-chips disambiguation HUD rather than relying on the confidence field. Never ask Jev for numbers, ordinals, counts, free text or dictation content; slice those in code and offer candidates. Keep all questions and thresholds in one reviewed file, build a labeled real-microphone utterance set before trusting any threshold, assert on decisions rather than exact probabilities in tests, pin the model version once tuned, and ship English only for v1. From Python, call POST https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/evaluate directly or point the typesafe-sdk at the Gateway's TypeSafe-compatible base URL.

lanes.summary: I benchmarked the local STT candidates on the target i5-8350U under CPython 3.14.7. Other lanes kept loadavg at 6 to 25 throughout, so every latency figure is pessimistic. Python 3.14 is not a blocker: moonshine-voice, sherpa-onnx, onnxruntime, onnx-asr, vosk, faster-whisper plus ctranslate2, and pywhispercpp all have cp314, abi3 or interpreter-independent wheels. Short commands do not need streaming ASR on this CPU. Buffer the utterance, endpoint it with push to talk release or a VAD, then decode once on ONE thread with sherpa-onnx. Parakeet TDT 110M int8 took a median 162 ms (394 MB RSS; NVIDIA card mean WER 7.49%). Moonshine Tiny took a median 120 ms (182 MB, MIT). More threads were slower under contention. moonshine-voice Tiny Streaming gives live partials and good keyterm biasing, but it ran near 100% of real time at about 386% CPU. Finalization took 190 to 715 ms after push to talk release and 640 to 1185 ms with its built-in VAD. Small Streaming, the NeMo 80 ms FastConformer (RTF 1.33) and Nemotron 0.6B streaming (RTF 5.4) are not viable. Parakeet 0.6B int8 offline needs a median 660 to 690 ms per command and 1.15 GB. The 2023 20M zipformer drops command onsets. VAD endpoint delay is min_silence plus 20 to 100 ms, and 300 to 400 ms is the practical floor. Decoding speculatively at about 180 ms of silence hides the endpoint wait behind Jev's 320 ms. sounddevice delivers audio every 10 to 21 ms. pw-record needs stdbuf -o0, otherwise the pipe delivers 128 ms bursts. Expected speech end to action is about 0.5 s with push to talk and 0.65 s with VAD.
lanes.recommendation:
1. Command path: use sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 on system Python 3.14 as the single speech runtime.
   - Capture with sounddevice at 16 kHz mono, blocksize 160 to 320, latency='low'. Keep the stream open all the time with a 400 ms pre-roll ring buffer.
   - Endpoint by push to talk release (Hyprland bind plus bindr) by default.
   - Alternative endpoint: Silero v5 VAD (MIT) in sherpa-onnx with min_silence of about 0.35 s. Add a speculative decode and a speculative Jev call at about 0.18 s of silence, so the endpoint wait overlaps Jev's 320 ms.
   - Decode the buffered utterance once with OfflineRecognizer at num_threads=1.
   - Default model: Parakeet TDT 110M int8. It measured about 160 ms and 394 MB here. It is CC-BY-4.0, and NVIDIA's card gives mean WER 7.49%.
   - Low-memory alternative: Moonshine Tiny non-streaming export. It measured about 120 ms and 182 MB here, and it is MIT.
   - Put the transcript, the N-best list and fuzzy-matched app and title candidates into the Jev state. Jev's choice questions then resolve entities, which makes recognizer-side biasing optional.
   - Expected speech end to action is about 0.5 s with push to talk and about 0.65 s with VAD.
   - Give Jev a hard 1 s timeout, and keep a local fallback for the top commands.
2. Dictation: run moonshine-voice Tiny Streaming only while dictation is active, because it burns several cores on this CPU. It gives live partials, and set_context with the focused window text biases it. For quality over liveness, load Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 int8 lazily and decode per VAD segment. That path measured RTF 0.34 to 0.41 and 1.15 GB here.
3. Fallbacks:
   - Kroko streaming zipformer with an external VAD and a 1.6 s zero-pad flush. It finalizes in 100 to 200 ms at 196 MB. Check the CC-BY-SA terms first.
   - Vosk small with a generated hard grammar, as a closed-set verifier.
4. Wake word: make it opt-in through sherpa-onnx KeywordSpotter. It is open vocabulary, needs no training and uses the same runtime. pymicro-wakeword is the alternative.
5. Avoid:
   - openWakeWord: it fails to install on 3.14 and its pretrained models are non-commercial.
   - TEN VAD, if license cleanliness matters.
   - Any 0.6B streaming model, the NeMo 80 ms FastConformer, Kyutai STT, and the Whisper family for commands.
6. Echo cancellation: ship none by default. Duck the default sink volume while push to talk is held. Document the PipeWire echo-cancel monitor.mode config as optional, with webrtc.transient_suppression on and gain_control off.
7. Cloud STT: use it only for long dictation. The gateway-stt lane owns the measured numbers, and I quote none here.
8. Re-run every benchmark on an idle machine with real microphone recordings before freezing the model choice.

corrections.claim: Non-streaming Moonshine Tiny decodes 1 s commands in median 120 ms (87 to 214) on 1 thread, RSS 182 MB, 8/8 correct
corrections.evidence: Stored bench_sherpa_mstiny_t1.json matches (median 119.5, 87 to 214, RSS 182, loadavg 16). t2 median 215.5, t4 median 281 also match. My rerun of bench_sherpa.py at loadavg 27.8, 1 thread: median 166 ms (123 to 372), RSS 183 MB, RTF 0.169.
corrections.correction: Latency is load-dependent: 120 ms at loadavg 16, 166 ms (max 372) at loadavg 27. '8 of 8 correct' is only true after normalization: hypotheses are 'Switch to Workspace 3.', 'Move window to workspace 2.', 'Toggle full screen.' (digits, casing, punctuation, 'full screen' split). The pipeline must normalize before building Jev state.

corrections.claim: Parakeet TDT 110M int8 decodes commands in median 162 ms (151 to 229) on 1 thread, RSS 394 MB, RTF 0.17, 8/8 correct
corrections.evidence: Stored bench_sherpa_p110_t1.json matches (median 161.5, 151 to 229, RSS 394, RTF 0.173, loadavg 16). My rerun at loadavg 27.4, 1 thread: median 511.5 ms (373 to 845), RTF 0.302, RSS 394 MB. Output included 'Focus, Kitty.' with a spurious comma.
corrections.correction: The 162 ms figure does not hold under heavier contention: 3.2x slowdown to about 510 ms at loadavg 27, versus 1.4x for Moonshine Tiny. Moonshine Tiny is the more robust pick on this CPU. NVIDIA model card figures were not re-checked.

lanes.summary: Recommendation for the voice HUD: a separate resident process in Python + GTK4 + gtk4-layer-shell (PyGObject 3.56.3 on system Python 3.14.7), fed by the engine over a Unix socket, with a Quickshell/QML frontend planned later for Omarchy 4 style desktops. Everything needed is already installed and was run live on this Hyprland 0.56.2 session. The layer-shell shim must be loaded before gi (CDLL("libgtk4-layer-shell.so")); without it the HUD becomes a normal tiled window and steals focus. Use two overlay-layer surfaces, namespaces hyprvoice-hud (pill) and hyprvoice-hints (full monitor, on demand), keyboard mode NONE, exclusive zone -1, empty input region. A second pass on 2026-09-21 closed open items: click-through verified by hover test with a control run and it survives resize; source confirms only overlay renders above fullscreen; runtime keyword layerrule re-applies to already mapped layers; layer rule animation values are unvalidated and non slide/popin means fade, so Omarchy's animation="none" is harmless; reserved order is left, top, right, bottom; gradient cap is 10. Layer rule effects are identical in hyprlang and Lua (blur, ignore_alpha, xray, no_anim, dim_around, animation, order, above_lock, no_screen_share, blur_popups); ignorezero and ignorealpha are gone. Use no_anim plus in-surface animation because rules cannot set speed. Default Vulkan GSK renderer holds 59 fps (p95 16.9 ms) on the UHD 620 when each frame is one Gsk.Path or one cairo context; per-node drawing from Python drops frames. Single-target highlight should use compositor setprop border color; client-drawn rings only for numbered hint mode, since no geometry-change event exists. Qt6 QML + layer-shell-qt also verified working here.
lanes.recommendation: Build the HUD as its own resident process in Python + GTK4 + gtk4-layer-shell, run with /usr/bin/python3 (PyGObject is a distro package, invisible to a default uv venv), started by a systemd user unit with GTK_A11Y=none. First lines of the entry module: CDLL("libgtk4-layer-shell.so") before import gi, then hard-fail if not Gtk4LayerShell.is_supported(). Create one hidden window per monitor and show with set_visible (about 9 ms to openlayer); never spawn per utterance. Key calls: LS.init_for_window, LS.set_namespace("hyprvoice-hud"), LS.set_layer(OVERLAY), LS.set_keyboard_mode(NONE), LS.set_anchor(BOTTOM), LS.set_margin, LS.set_exclusive_zone(-1), LS.set_monitor(gdk_monitor matched by get_connector()), and on every map surface.set_input_region(cairo.Region()). Remove the "background" CSS class and add your CssProvider at PRIORITY_USER + 1, because the user's HyDE gtk.css otherwise paints the transparent corners. At startup probe hyprctl -j status, then install rules in the right dialect: hyprlang one-liner via keyword ("blur on, ignore_alpha 0.35, xray off, no_anim on, match:namespace ^hyprvoice-hud$") or named hl.layer_rule via eval built with lua_str(); re-install on configreloaded. Never set no_screen_share (it blacks out grim) and never blur the full-monitor hints surface. Read the look over the request socket in one [[BATCH]] and reuse the user's border gradient, rounding and windows bezier with a fixed 120 to 160 ms duration. Draw the waveform as one Gsk.Path + append_stroke (or one append_cairo), drive it with add_tick_callback and remove the callback when idle; keep the default Vulkan renderer. Flash the target window with setprop active_border_color and unset; use client-drawn rings and numbered badges only in short-lived hint mode, polling j/clients while visible. Filter hyprvoice-* namespaces out of hypruse's layer snapshot and wait_for. Keep the NDJSON HUD protocol frontend-neutral so a Quickshell/QML frontend can follow.

corrections.claim: PyGObject 3.56.3 works under Python 3.14.7 with GTK 4.22.4 + gtk4-layer-shell 1.3.0; layer-shell lib must be loaded before import gi
corrections.evidence: Local: python 3.14.7, gi 3.56.3, pacman gtk4 4.22.4, gtk4-layer-shell 1.3.0. Gtk4LayerShell.is_supported() = False without preload, True with CDLL('libgtk4-layer-shell.so') before import gi. pygobject NEWS 3.54.0: 'Fix compatibility with Python 3.14 (mr 433)'.
corrections.correction: Core facts confirmed. Not re-verified (would map a window): HUD at level 3 520x96 without focus, and the fallback becoming a focus-taking tiled toplevel.

corrections.claim: getoption colon form, gaps as custom '5 5 5 5', gradient 'ffa4a4a4 ff4e4e4e 45deg', animations [animations, beziers] with overridden; socket batch of 11 p50 0.60 ms vs 16.6 ms hyprctl
corrections.evidence: Re-measured: general:border_size ok, general.border_size 'no such option'; gradient string identical; animations is a 2-list, layersIn not overridden, global speed 8.0. My 11-query batch p50 0.17 ms, j/clients 0.33 ms, hyprctl subprocess 17.4 ms at load avg 11.
corrections.correction: '5 5 5 5' is gaps_out; gaps_in is '2 2 2 2'. Batch latency is query-mix dependent (0.17 to 0.60 ms); the two orders of magnitude gap to subprocess holds.

lanes.summary: Surveyed Talon, Cursorless, numen, Linux dictation tools, Serenade, Apple Voice Control, Windows and Android Voice Access, Dragon, four 2026 Hyprland voice projects, and seven public projects that already pair Jev with voice or UI control. Findings: (1) window-management vocabulary is stable across vendors (open, switch to or focus, close window, minimize, maximize, snap, show numbers, show grid, go to sleep, wake up, undo that, scratch that, what can I say), so copy it and let Jev absorb paraphrase. (2) Every mature system disambiguates with numbered overlays plus a spoken number, never a spoken question; Serenade acts on the top guess and lets a spoken number swap it, which suits Jev choice probabilities and hypruse marks. (3) Jev voice projects, including devfros/omause for Omarchy, converged independently on closed-set choices, code-extracted spans that Jev selects, gate booleans is_command, complete and destructive, thresholds in code, numbered overlays on low confidence, a spoken confirm for destructive actions, and a deterministic local fast path. (4) Endpointing silence dominates perceived latency (Talon 300 ms default; Jev apps 550 to 900 ms); literature targets are acknowledgement within 100 ms, about 400 ms (Doherty), and 1 s for flow. (5) Open mic misfires (0.95 misactivations per hour, Dubois 2020), so default to hold to talk through Hyprland bind and bindr, with an opt-in hands-free mode using the Talon sleep grammar. (6) No surveyed system offers real undo for window actions, and none of the Jev or Hyprland projects found has sleep grammar or a help overlay, or combines Wayland with an accessibility tree. The report ends with 16 prioritized UX principles. No Jev latency was measured by us.
lanes.recommendation:
Build the app as a silent input layer that reuses the established voice vocabulary and the architecture the Jev voice projects have converged on, then add what none of them has.

1. **Activation.** Default to hold to talk through Hyprland `bind` plus `bindr` calling CLI verbs on a daemon. Key release is then the endpoint, which removes the endpointing delay and avoids false accepts. Ship tap to latch. Add an opt-in hands-free mode that copies Talon's sleep grammar (go to sleep with trailing phrase swallow, anchored wake up, deep sleep, idle auto-sleep) and an 8 s follow-up window. Add echo cancellation and a local gate so non-command speech never leaves the machine.

2. **Decision layer.**
   - Try a deterministic local fast path first.
   - Otherwise send one Jev request per utterance with a closed-set intent choice (synonyms and negative examples in the option descriptions), target choices over live windows, workspaces, apps and binds, and the booleans `is_command`, `complete`, `compound` and `destructive`.
   - Keep thresholds in one config file and pin the model version.

3. **Disambiguation.** Show numbered layer-shell badges on candidate windows and resolve the spoken number locally. Act first with a number swap for reversible actions. Reuse hypruse `marks` and `click_ui` as "show numbers here".

4. **Safety.** Risk tiers live in code. Dangerous options are hidden from the model and the executor fails closed. Tier 1 actions such as close need a standalone "confirm" or a click, with a timeout that cancels.

5. **Differentiators.**
   - A real undo journal of inverse compositor actions.
   - Repeaters ("again", "twice").
   - Chaining through hypruse `sequence` and `wait_for`, with "it" bound to the new window.
   - A "what can I say" overlay that includes the user's own keybinds.
   - `teach --last` alias learning and STT biasing with live window and app names.

6. **Feedback.** A non-focusable, click-through HUD pill plus a Waybar module with about six states. Always show the heard text and the chosen action. Offer four optional earcons and no speech by default.

7. **Latency budget.** Acknowledge within 100 ms. Show a visible effect within 1 s of end of speech, aiming for 400 ms on closed-set commands. Make the endpoint delay user configurable.

lanes.summary: hypruse 0.11.0 (commit 9a84bdb) is importable as a library today. All 15 tools are plain synchronous functions in src/hypruse/server.py, wrapped only by a journal decorator that is a passthrough when HYPRUSE_JOURNAL is unset. Importing hypruse.server never imports mcp: a cold process pays about 95 ms (65 ms over a bare interpreter) on venv 3.13 or system 3.14.7 with zero third-party packages, versus 0.7 to 0.9 s for the FastMCP build. verbs.run is the reference in-process path but must not be reused in a daemon because it mutates os.environ and takes per-call file locks. The dominant cost is transport: every query and dispatch forks the hyprctl binary (about 20 ms median, 11 ms floor), while the same six-query snapshot over the raw .socket.sock takes 0.3 ms and parses with the existing snapshot_from. a11y spawns one busctl per D-Bus call (hundreds per window), and the AT-SPI registry on this machine is broken, so no walk could be timed. Safety gaps matter more for voice than for MCP: the lock check is a /proc name scan that fails open, covers only pointer, keyboard and click_ui, and Hyprland itself does not lock-gate IPC dispatch; hyprctl locked exists and stays true after a locker crash (verified in Hyprland 0.56.2 source). HYPRUSE_READONLY and HYPRUSE_CLIPBOARD are not enforced for library callers. HYPRUSE_STRICT is hostile to voice use. State is process-global (env flags, _last_marks, _vp, _provider, beacon files shared with four running hypruse MCP servers), so acting calls need a single worker. HYPRUSE_SEAT is dead code that still forces a virtual pointer to be created for keyboard-only work. The snapshot lacks focusHistoryID, workspace names and initialClass, which a voice resolver will want.
lanes.recommendation: Fork hypruse as a library, not as a subprocess or MCP client. Boot sequence in the daemon, on the main thread before any GLib or asyncio loop: session.ensure_session_env(), server.use_plain_blocks(), safety.init() (after renaming the runtime directory away from $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypruse so it stops sharing files with the user's running hypruse MCP servers), safety.on_shutdown(input.release_held), optional journal.start. Then call server.hypr, server.launch, server.use_bind, server.keyboard and friends directly, and map results to delivered, refused, no_result, error with verbs.exit_for plus the exception classes. Do not call verbs.run. First three code changes, in order of payoff: (1) replace the body of hyprctl._run with a raw .socket.sock client (flags + '/' + args, [[BATCH]] for batches, raise HyprctlError on connection failure so guards keep failing closed); tests already patch at _run. This cuts a snapshot from about 20 ms to about 0.3 ms and makes a persistent world model trivial: one socket2 reader thread using events.parse_event, re-pulling the snapshot on change, so Jev state is already built when speech ends. Add a second pure builder beside snapshot_from that keeps focusHistoryID, workspace names and initialClass and sanitizes titles. (2) Replace trust.session_locked with the j/locked query, keep the /proc scan only as a fallback, fail closed when unreadable, and add one daemon-level gate that drops utterances (ideally stops capture) while locked, because hypr, launch and use_bind have no lock check and Hyprland does not gate IPC dispatch. Also re-implement the READONLY and CLIPBOARD gates in the fork's wrapper. (3) Delete HYPRUSE_SEAT and VirtualKeyboard, which removes the forced virtual pointer creation on keyboard-only calls. Run every acting call on one dedicated worker thread, treat HYPRUSE_* env flags as boot-time config only, leave HYPRUSE_STRICT off, never pass allow_auth=True from voice, and give the HUD a layer namespace that classifies as unknown. Treat click_ui and ui as off the hot path until a11y.py is ported to a persistent Gio or Atspi connection and the user's AT-SPI bus is repaired. Drop the MCP surface, skill, screenshot, zoom and marks image path, cli_state and the PyPI release workflow from the fork.

corrections.claim: Importing hypruse.server does not import mcp/pydantic/anyio/httpx; cold-process import is 97 ms (venv 3.13) and 93 ms (system 3.14.7) versus 704 ms for server.app() and 933 ms for import mcp.types; pyproject lists only mcp.
corrections.evidence: Structure confirmed on system Python 3.14.7 with PYTHONPATH=src: after import, none of mcp, pydantic, pydantic_core, anyio, httpx, starlette is in sys.modules; only site-packages module loaded is _distutils_hack (setuptools .pth). pyproject.toml:23 is dependencies = ["mcp>=1.2,<2"], :6 requires-python >=3.11. Absolute timings NOT reproduced: at loadavg 17 to 18.6, n=9 cold processes, I got bare 67 ms (3.14) / 57 ms (3.13), import hypruse.server 239 ms median / 213 min (3.14) and 183 ms / 172 min (3.13), server.app() 1,923 ms, import mcp.types 2,875 ms. Child CPU time via wait4 agreed (219 ms import on 3.14, 1,659 ms app()).
corrections.correction: Quote the import as 0.1 to 0.25 s cold depending on machine load, and 8x to 10x cheaper than building FastMCP. The ratio is stable across passes, the absolute ms are not. Python 3.14 was slower than 3.13 in my run (239 vs 183 ms), the reverse of the researcher's 93 vs 97, so treat the interpreters as equivalent. The zero-third-party-dependency conclusion and Python 3.14.7 viability hold.

lanes.summary: Researched the Hyprland 0.56.2 control surface from the tagged source, release notes, locally installed files and read-only live measurements. Direct socket requests from Python cost 0.05 to 0.16 ms p50 versus about 6 ms (p95 9 ms, max 16 ms) for spawning hyprctl; a full eight-query [[BATCH]] snapshot of about 11 KB takes 0.44 ms p50. The protocol is one request per connection, flags before a slash (j, r, a, c), batch replies joined by three newlines, dispatch replies "ok" or an error string. The compositor polls an accepted connection for up to 5 seconds on its main thread, so a client must send immediately. In 0.56 the legacy string dispatchers (71 names) are a translator over a typed action core shared with the new Lua config. Under the Lua provider, "dispatch X" is evaluated as hl.dispatch(X), so legacy strings fail; j/status reports the provider (hyprlang here). Source text says .conf support will be removed in 0.57, so a Lua renderer is mandatory. togglesplit and swapsplit were removed in 0.54 in favour of layoutmsg; workspaceopt and setignoregrouplock are dead. Window selectors use RE2 FullMatch and first match wins, so always target address:0x or stableid:. socket2 has 45 events, no lock events, 64-event client queue, addresses without 0x. IPC dispatch is not gated by session lock; the locked request exists (0.09 ms) and must gate every action. "ok" does not prove effect for stale selectors. Window and workspace animations here run 500 to 600 ms and dominate perceived latency. The report includes a 48-row voice operation table with legacy and Lua strings, target needs and destructiveness.
lanes.recommendation: Replace hypruse's hyprctl subprocess transport with a direct stdlib socket client in the daemon: build the full request, connect, sendall, shutdown(SHUT_WR), read to EOF, never hold an idle connection. Take state with one [[BATCH]] snapshot (locked first, then j/status, clients, workspaces, monitors, activewindow, activeworkspace, layers; about 0.44 ms) and keep it fresh from a dedicated non-blocking socket2 reader so the Jev state string is ready when speech ends; resnapshot on reconnect and on configreloaded. Resolve targets in the Jev choice step against the snapshot and always dispatch with address:0x (prepend 0x to event addresses), never class or title regex. Keep two renderers per operation (legacy string and hl.dsp Lua expression) selected by j/status.configProvider, because 0.56.2 announces .conf removal in 0.57 and legacy dispatch strings stop working under the Lua provider; reuse hypruse's existing provider probe and lua_str escaping. Refuse all actions when locked is true since IPC dispatch bypasses the lock screen. Treat "ok" as accepted and confirm effects via the matching socket2 event. Send compound commands as one batch. Require elevated Jev confidence plus explicit confirmation for killwindow/forcekillactive and exit, moderate gating for closewindow, sendshortcut, dpms off and exec (allowlist). Do not write a compositor plugin. Offer an opt-in snappy animation profile (2 to 3 ds for windows, windowsMove, workspaces) since the current 500 to 600 ms tweens dominate perceived latency; validate the per-action animation toggle idea live before using it.

corrections.claim: Direct AF_UNIX requests take 0.095 ms p50 (j/activewindow) and 0.161 ms p50 (j/clients, 6.2 KB) vs 5.99/6.04 ms p50 for spawning hyprctl (p95 8 to 9 ms).
corrections.evidence: Own benchmark script, read-only: direct socket p50 0.113 ms (n=300) and 0.267 ms (j/clients 6247 bytes, n=100), p95 0.18/0.43 ms. hyprctl -j activewindow spawn measured 15.3 ms p50, 22.4 ms p95 (n=50), about 2.5x the claim, likely machine load from other benchmarks.
corrections.correction: Direct socket is well under 1 ms (0.1 to 0.3 ms p50); hyprctl spawn is load dependent, 6 to 20 ms p50. Conclusion (use the socket directly) holds and is strengthened.

lanes.summary: Three of the eight gateway transcription models stream partials: spacexai/grok-stt, openai/gpt-realtime-whisper and google/gemini-3.5-transcribe-live. They are exactly the models tagged websocket-transcription in the catalog, and Vercel's speech to text doc names the same three. The other five are batch only through the gateway. The wire protocol was read from the shipped TypeScript source of @ai-sdk/gateway 4.0.87 and matches Vercel's docs. Batch is POST https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v4/ai/transcription-model with base64 JSON (multipart unsupported), model chosen by the ai-model-id header, and Vercel documents a stdlib Python example. Streaming is a WebSocket on the same path with ?ai-model-id=, auth carried in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, one JSON start frame, binary PCM frames of at most 64 KiB, a JSON audio-done frame, then JSON stream parts ending in finish. Realtime uses /realtime-model plus a minted vcst_ token, has 5 minute idle and 25 minute session limits, and is the wrong tool here. Pricing is USD per second of audio for five models (0.06 to 0.57 USD per thousand 2 s commands); the 1e-10 input values look like placeholders (inference). No vendor publishes numeric latency. The only independent numbers (Pipecat, direct to provider, not via gateway) are 458 ms median for Gemini live and 740 ms for gpt-realtime-whisper; grok-stt is unmeasured. Local Moonshine tiny measured about 235 ms to final after push to talk release on this machine (another lane's benchmark, synthetic audio, loaded machine). With Jev at 321 ms, local totals about 0.56 s against an estimated 0.8 to 1.2 s for the best gateway path. No live calls were made, and gateway speech to text is beta with gated rollout, so team access is unconfirmed.
lanes.recommendation:
Keep speech to text local on the hot path. On current evidence no gateway model meets the owner's "blazing fast" bar. Local Moonshine tiny finalizes about 235 ms after push to talk release (measured on this machine, synthetic audio). The best gateway option is estimated at 0.5 to 0.9 s, and Jev adds 321 ms to either.

Ranked gateway options:
1. google/gemini-3.5-transcribe-live over the streaming WebSocket. It has the only good independent number (458 ms median, 599 ms P99, direct to provider). It accepts customVocabulary and requires 16 kHz PCM16.
2. spacexai/grok-stt streaming. It is unmeasured, so it cannot honestly rank first, but benchmark it next because it may win. It is 3 to 10 times cheaper, flushes explicitly on audio.done (good for push to talk), supports keyterm biasing and endpointing down to 0, and has zero data retention. Its partials arrive only about every 500 ms.
3. openai/gpt-realtime-whisper with streaming.delay "minimal". It measured 740 ms at the default delay. It is the most expensive and has no vocabulary biasing in streaming mode.
4. Batch models, as a fallback only. Use grok-stt over POST and avoid the three OpenAI batch models, which the catalog deprecates on 2027-02-26.
5. Realtime type models: do not use.

Use gateway speech to text as a gated second opinion. When Jev's confidence on the local transcript is low, resend the buffered clip to the gateway and ask Jev again.

Promote option 1 or 2 to the hot path only if real microphone tests show tiny is not accurate enough. In that case gateway streaming would beat the local "small" model (about 1.0 s) on both speed and accuracy.

Before building on any of this, the main loop must do two things with the real key. First, confirm the team has beta access to gateway speech to text. Second, benchmark the three streaming models (n >= 30, median and P95) on socket open to stream-start, first audio byte to first partial, and audio-done to finish.

corrections.claim: Streaming wire protocol: wss .../v4/ai/transcription-model?ai-model-id=, subprotocols ai-gateway-transcription.v1 + ai-gateway-auth.<token>, start frame, binary frames <=64 KiB (256 KiB reject), audio-done, listed server parts; experimental and only in SDK source
corrections.evidence: gateway-transcription-model.ts:184-191 (URL), 217 (64 KiB), gateway-realtime-auth.ts constants, transcription-stream-envelope.ts rules 1-7 all match. Vercel doc documents only experimental_streamTranscribe, no raw WS.
corrections.correction: Part union also includes a 'raw' part (stream-part.ts:76); start frame may also carry providerOptions and includeRawChunks (lines 140-148). Client must ignore unknown part types (envelope rule 6).

corrections.claim: Long lived API key rides in ai-gateway-auth.<token> on the server side SDK path, so a Python daemon need not mint a vcst_ secret; mint route POST /v1/realtime/client-secrets {model, routeKind, expiresIn}, single use, 60 s default, 300 s max
corrections.evidence: Code reading confirmed: getProtocolsFromHeaders lines 200-214 slices Bearer into the subprotocol; mint body at gateway-provider.ts:376-390; 60/300 s and single use confirmed in Vercel doc and provider.ts:217.
corrections.correction: Server acceptance of a long lived key on the WS route is unverifiable without a key, and the auth module requires the token to fit the RFC subprotocol token grammar. Build plan should include a fallback that mints a vcst_ token per session.

corrections.claim: Local Moonshine tiny reaches final a median 234 to 243 ms after PTT stop (n=8, range 61-463), VAD 780-943, small 1036 ms, CPU 83-119% of a core, under loadavg 11-16
corrections.evidence: Recomputed from bench_tiny.json (ptt 234.0, vad 942.5, load 118.8%), bench_tiny05.json (243.0, 780.0, 83.0%), bench_small.json (1035.5): all match.
corrections.correction: Report omits bench_tiny_quiet.json and bench_small_quiet.json in the same scratchpad: at lower load (loadavg 10.4/4.8/4.0) tiny PTT median is 383.5 ms (260-715), small 885 ms. Honest local time to final is about 0.25 to 0.4 s; end to end about 0.56 to 0.70 s. Local still beats gateway estimates.

lanes.summary: (research agent died before returning; the complete report on disk is reused)

contradictions: Streaming partials vs one-shot decode: nlu-arch and gateway-stt build the hot path on streaming ASR with stable partials, n-best and speculation on partials (345 ms / 0.25 s figures); the stt lane measured streaming as unviable on this CPU and recommends buffered offline decode with no partials. The ui 'hearing' state and prior-art's 'partial transcript within 100 ms' also assume partials. Adaptive 'partial already parses' endpointing cannot exist under the stt recommendation.

STT model default has three answers: stt report says Parakeet TDT 110M, the stt verifier says Moonshine Tiny is more robust (Parakeet slowed 3.2x to 511 ms under load), gateway-stt says moonshine-voice Tiny Streaming.

N-best and biasing: jev-design ('alternatives' in state) and stt ('pass N-best') need alternatives, but the offline Moonshine path in sherpa-onnx is greedy only and hotwords are transducer only and inconclusive on Parakeet.

Latency budgets disagree: nlu-arch assumes ASR finalize 40 ms, PTT action 45 to 60 ms, Jev 150 to 250 ms; measured decode is 120 to 166 ms (372 to 845 under load) and Jev 321 ms. stt says 0.5 s PTT / 0.65 s VAD, gateway-stt 0.56 to 0.70 s. prior-art's 400 ms goal is unreachable on the Jev path.
Four different Jev deadlines: nlu-arch 450 ms (would drop roughly the slowest tenth of healthy calls at live p90 356 to 439 ms), stt 1 s, jev-design 600 to 900 ms, jev-wire 1.5 s.

One request per utterance with at most one in flight (jev-design, prior-art) vs nlu-arch's state-sliced R1/R2/R3 plus per-clause sets plus hedges (6 streams, 4 speculative sets). Live data on disk: 3 concurrent costs about 45 ms more and large requests are the ones that 503.

App candidates: fuzzy prefilter to top 10 to 15 (jev-design, prior-art) vs all 86 apps plus a roughly 180-option joint action Choice (nlu-arch). A lexical prefilter removes exactly the semantic cases ('the browser') Jev is for; neither side has accuracy data.
Default route: jev-wire recommends route B (/typesafe/v1/systemone), nlu-arch uses route A (/v1/evaluate). Live A 335 ms vs B 316 ms p50 at n=30 is within noise.
Keepalive: nlu-arch pings every 20 to 30 s while armed, jev-wire warms on PTT press with keepalive_expiry 120; the edge idle timeout is unknown so neither is grounded.

Memoization and dead bands vs live noise: nlu-arch claims local memoization gives determinism and uses a 0.05 dead band and 0.15 margin; dayone_out.json shows 30 identical requests moving P(target) 0.45 to 0.67 with the argmax flipping 4 of 30 times (the brief's 0.50 to 0.59 was only the first 6 reps). Caching one sample freezes a coin flip and margin gates will flicker.

Destructive actions: jev-design auto-acts R2 at >= 0.9; nlu-arch never on Jev alone plus 1.5 s countdown; prior-art always holds for a standalone spoken confirm and hides session/system actions from the model entirely, while nlu-arch and jev-design put close, exit and power in the intent Choice. Tier membership of launch and typing also differs.

Ambiguity policy: prior-art P0 says act on the top guess and let a number swap it (Serenade) for reversible actions; nlu-arch and jev-design say do not act, show numbered hints. prior-art itself notes the undo this depends on does not exist yet.

HUD contract: ui says bottom center, one-way display-only, permanently empty input region; prior-art says top center, click-through except while a confirm card is up, and a HUD click as the non-voice confirm path.

PTT transport: stt and prior-art use bind/bindr that exec a CLI verb; hypruse-map measured a cold Python CLI start at 95 to 240 ms, which lands on the endpoint at key release. hypr-ipc's event dispatcher plus socket2 custom>> avoids the spawn but no lane connected them. bindr was never exercised live (0 release binds configured).
Echo cancellation: stt says off by default (duck during PTT); nlu-arch lists AEC as injection hardening and prior-art wants it for hands-free.

Lua provider: hypr-ipc says two renderers are mandatory (.conf removal notice for 0.57); hypruse-map lists keeping Lua as an open question; ui and hypr-ipc executed zero Lua strings. The mandatory path is fully unexecuted.

Interpreter and packaging: ui requires the system interpreter for PyGObject; stt says sherpa-onnx 'on system Python' but benchmarked from a venv (Arch system Python is externally managed); hypruse-map wants an a11y rewrite on system gi. The engine needs pip-only wheels and possibly system-only gi; no lane resolves it.

Vendor 'size barely matters' (relayed by jev-wire, jev-design) vs live dayone data: p50 315 ms at 725 tokens, 448 ms at 6k, 544 ms at 11.5k, and 13 of 30 HTTP 503 at 11.5k. nlu-arch's 6k-token speculative sets sit in the degraded zone.

Inferred confidence formula (p_max - 1/n)/(1 - 1/n) from jev-design and nlu-arch: holds on all 21 live Choice answers, fails on all 7 live Score answers (formula 0.68, service 0.75). 'Compute confidence client side' is wrong for Score.

Minor: hyprctl spawn cost 6 ms (hypr-ipc) vs 15 to 22 ms elsewhere; hypruse-map's 'every postEvent name' list omits 8 events that ui and hypr-ipc found (conclusion 'no lock event' still holds); hypruse-map's open question on when 'hyprctl locked' shipped is answered by hypr-ipc (commit dated 2024-05-13, date not rechecked).
unverified_load_bearing: Jev window-target accuracy. Every lane assumes Jev absorbs paraphrase and ASR errors. The only live data point is bad: 'put the browser on workspace three' with one Firefox window scored 0.45 to 0.67 and picked the focused kitty 4 of 30 times. design.py and overlap.py were written to fix the question design but their output was not saved to disk.
Jev on real ASR output (homophones, split words, Moonshine's 'Workspace 3.' casing and digits): not found in any source, never tested.
All act/confirm/reject thresholds, margins and dead bands: vendor cookbooks (some on jev-1.12) and third-party READMEs for other domains; live noise of about 0.2 invalidates the margin arithmetic.

Model pinning through the gateway is unknown AND the gateway response hides the version (both routes return model 'typesafe-ai/jev', direct returns 'jev-1.13.0'), so nlu-arch's cache invalidation on response.model cannot detect alias drift.
Prompt-injection resistance: one vendor sentence and one third-party anecdote; no adversarial-title test, in state or in criteria.
503 mechanism (size, rate, or promo capacity), whether an immediate retry succeeds, whether route B differs; one account, one morning.
Tail latency (p95/p99) at production request size over hours; whether hedging helps or just doubles load on a service already returning 503.
HTTP/2 idle timeout at the Vercel edge and first-call cost after suspend/resume.
Billing after 2026-09-25 (all live calls show cost 0 under the promo), zero-balance error shape, free-tier eligibility for other users, abort billing.
Direct TypeSafe path: no key, zero comparative data. Live provider leg is about 220 of 315 ms, so 'direct would be about 280 to 300 ms' is inference.
STT accuracy and latency: 8 clean synthetic TTS clips at loadavg 6 to 27; no real microphone, noise, accent, rare app names, or idle-machine run. '8 of 8' needed normalization.
350 ms commit and 180 ms speculative endpoint: design estimate, no human data.
No lane ever sent a dispatch over the raw socket. Wire spelling, 'ok' on stale addresses, the 1023-byte-multiple hang and the 5 s main-thread stall are all from source reading.
Every Lua-provider string (dispatch expressions, hl.layer_rule, set_prop, exec rules) is unexecuted; several field names were not even read.
Per-action animation suppression is untested and impossible under Lua as written; the 500 to 600 ms tween is the largest visible cost.
All acting latencies and all a11y timings. AT-SPI registry broken on this machine since 2026-09-13, so ui, marks, click_ui, nlu-arch's R3 and the strict password guard cannot be measured or demoed.
Session-lock behavior of individual dispatchers, and the locked gate under Omarchy 4's Quickshell locker.
HUD at fractional scale and multi-monitor, a real click through the surface, blur cost, scanout loss under fullscreen video, SIGTERM under a busy GTK loop.
Option-order bias and question independence: the live tests (0.68 to 0.83 across permutations; 0.57 alone vs 0.53 among 20, n=8) cannot be separated from the 0.2 identical-request noise.
uncovered_risks: Privacy of state sent to the cloud: window titles (mail subjects, page titles, chat names, private-browsing and password-manager titles) and, via R3, a11y labels and possibly field values go from an EU machine through Vercel to TypeSafe in AWS us-west-2 on every utterance, multiplied by speculation and hedging. Catalog says zdr all / no_training all and a zeroDataRetention option exists, but no lane analyzed gateway observability storage, whether the option is per request or works on route B, or TypeSafe's terms. No redaction rules, denylist, or 'what was sent' inspector. Local cassettes, negative cache and JSONL history also persist transcripts and titles.

Third-party speech: in open-mic mode other people's speech is transcribed and sent to a cloud service; gateway-stt's fallback would send raw audio. The 'local gate' principle is stated but never specified.

Offline and degraded operation is one sentence in nlu-arch. No design for fast offline detection, captive portals, dead connection after resume, high 503 rates, zero credits, or single-vendor risk on a 6 day old model behind an experimental API. TypeSafe's LLM-backed adapter was mentioned as a fallback but never evaluated.

Microphone handling: no OS permission prompt on native Arch, so the app is the only honest indicator; stt's always-open capture stream (even with PTT) keeps mic indicators lit, blocks device suspend, and on Bluetooth headsets forces HSP/HFP and degrades playback permanently. Hardware mic mute, source hot-plug and a hard mic kill switch are undesigned.

Voice is an unauthenticated channel: no speaker verification considered; room audio, videos or web pages can speak commands and also say 'confirm'. Paths to arbitrary execution are not risk-ranked: launch takes a shell string, type_text into a terminal plus Enter, and use_bind can run any of 131 user binds (exec scripts, power menu, exit), all offered to Jev as options by nlu-arch.

Prompt injection beyond intent: nlu-arch's lexical anchor protects the intent tier only. A hostile title can steer the TARGET (focus, close, or dictation typed into the attacker's window). The live probe puts 'class: title' in option descriptions, the highest-leverage spot. a11y labels and notification text are equally untrusted. No structural defense proposed, none tested.
Speech-derived strings under the Lua provider are evaluated inside the compositor; only one argument has an injection blacklist today.
API key handling: no lane says where the gateway key lives, how it stays out of logs, cassettes and bug reports, or what a leak can spend.

Auth prompts: hypruse's interlock is blind to Quickshell polkit (Omarchy 4) and the strict password-field guard depends on the broken a11y bus; dictation into auth prompts and secrets in logs are open.

Licensing not consolidated: fork is fine (hypruse is MIT, owner holds copyright), but Parakeet is CC-BY-4.0 (attribution if bundled or auto-downloaded), Kroko CC-BY-SA unverified, TEN VAD not OSI clean, openWakeWord models non-commercial, GTK/PyGObject/Qt LGPL. Model distribution and checksums, earcon assets, and whether TypeSafe/Vercel terms allow a redistributed bring-your-own-key desktop controller were not checked.

Naming: ui hardcoded 'hyprvoice' (namespaces, unit, app id) while prior-art lists hyprvoice as an existing archived Hyprland project with 273 stars. No GitHub/AUR/PyPI check for any name; 'Jev' or 'TypeSafe' in the name would be a third-party mark; HYPRUSE_* env prefix also needs renaming.
Power and thermals on a 15 W laptop: always-open capture, continuous VAD, keepalive pings, socket2 reader, 10 to 20 Hz hint polling, resident GTK process; idle draw never measured.
Non-native English: Jev is English first, Moonshine Tiny English only; the owner's accent was never tested and no lane treats it as go/no-go.
Test infrastructure: no labeled utterance corpus, no ambient false-accept corpus; Hyprland integration tests need a QEMU virtio-gpu VM.
Coexistence: a voice daemon and the four running hypruse MCP agents acting on the same cursor and focus at the same moment was not considered.
Onboarding cost for other users of a published app (Vercel account, credits once the promo ends 2026-09-25) was not considered.
weakest_decisions: STT architecture and model (offline one-shot Moonshine Tiny or Parakeet 110M vs streaming with partials). Evidence is 8 synthetic TTS clips on a loaded machine, no real mic, accent or noise, and three lanes disagree. This choice also decides whether speculation on partials, adaptive endpointing, n-best and the HUD live transcript can exist. Fix: record 100 to 200 real commands on the laptop mic and run all three on an idle machine.

Jev question design and gating (one request vs sliced, prefilter vs full option lists, thresholds, margins, dead bands, memoization). Evidence is vendor cookbooks and week-old READMEs from other domains; the only live accuracy point is bad (0.45 to 0.67 on an easy target, 4 of 30 wrong), live noise is about four times the assumed dead band, large requests 503, and the model version can be neither pinned nor observed through the gateway. Freeze nothing before a labeled replay set exists.

Activation, endpointing and latency budget (hold-to-talk default via exec-based bindr, 350 ms commit with 180 ms speculative trigger, 0.5 s / 0.65 s totals, deadlines from 450 ms to 1.5 s). All design estimates: bindr never exercised, the exec CLI path adds a Python cold start to the endpoint, human pause tolerance unmeasured, no idle-machine numbers, and the 500 to 600 ms compositor animation has no tested mitigation.
Runner up: gateway vs direct TypeSafe as primary route (no direct key, zero comparative data), and how much Lua-provider work to do now (mandatory per source text, fully unexecuted).
needs_live_key: Rerun jevlive/design.py and overlap.py with output saved; then window-target accuracy on a labeled set of at least 100 utterances (semantic references, deictics, same-class windows) across question designs.
Adversarial window titles: intent steering and target steering, titles in state vs in criteria, with and without the 'reference data' note.
Model ids typesafe-ai/jev-1.13.0, jev-1.13.0, typesafe-ai/jev-latest, jev; inspect response headers for any version string since the body only says typesafe-ai/jev.
503 rate vs input tokens from 2k to 12k in 1k steps on both routes, with one immediate retry and its success rate.
Tail latency: several hundred calls at the real request size across a day, p95/p99, hedged vs not.
HTTP/2 idle timeout: one call after 30 s, 60 s, 2, 5, 15 min idle and after suspend/resume (verify-jev-wire/idle_probe.py exists).
Noise near thresholds: how many identical copies make the decision (not the probability) stable, and the token cost; live self-ensemble of 8 only cut stdev 0.059 to 0.040.
Option-order bias and question independence with at least 30 repeats per condition to beat the 0.2 noise.
Real ASR transcripts from a recorded mic corpus as state, with and without alternatives.
providerOptions.gateway.zeroDataRetention on both routes: accepted, and any latency or availability effect.
After 2026-09-25: confirm cost becomes nonzero and capture the zero-balance error shape on a throwaway key; free-tier eligibility for other users.
Abort billing: cancel 50 in-flight requests and compare reported usage.
Only if cloud STT fallback stays in scope: team beta access, raw key in the WebSocket subprotocol, audio-done to finish latency for grok-stt, gemini-3.5-transcribe-live, gpt-realtime-whisper.
Needs a second credential (TypeSafe direct key): latency from this machine, pinning to jev-1.13.0, fallback path.
